correctness.rationale: An initial color class of nonbridge vertices in a clique evolves monochromatically: all its members share the same state, and when at state 2, excluding oneself from the neighborhood does not affect the presence of blinking state 1. Hence the two bridge colors and the at most six initial nonbridge color cohorts yield an exact, size-independent dynamical quotient. Exhaustive deterministic enumeration of all 3^2(2^3-1)^2=441 admissible initial templates yields first synchronization at time 0..9 and exactly the stated ten 3-by-3 coefficient matrices, maximum 9. The four-block explicit 10-stage trace is an extremal witness for every pair of orders at least 2. Inclusion-exclusion counts onto maps from the labelled interior vertices to their nonempty supports, yielding the formulas for all a,b. A separate vertex-level C++ implementation checked all 1,185,921 colourings for a,b in 2..6, with matching counts. The proof is finite quotient enumeration after a proven exact reduction, not extrapolation from finite graph sizes. Neither program is independently externally audited.

originality.rationale: The specified inhibitory rule and its tree/path synchronization results were established by Lyu (arXiv:1407.1103; arXiv:1610.00837). Comparison of the inspected primary manuscript sections and the matched published/owned results identifies no theorem for two complete cliques joined by exactly one bridge with a nine-step all-input cutoff and the ten exact first-entry matrices. The previously reported 3-color results on complete bipartite or complete split graphs have different neighborhood structures; the earlier bridge-clique result applies to a different, excitatory transition rule. Only the new bridged-clique classification and distribution are asserted; possible unindexed equivalent work remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed earlier article, thesis or unpublished equivalent analysis could cover this exact graph/rule; database retrieval is not an exhaustive historical priority proof.

value.rationale: The single bridge is a natural graph-theoretic bottleneck between otherwise completely connected communities. It is nontrivial that every initial 3-color inhibitory configuration globally synchronizes within a constant number of updates independent of both clique sizes, particularly in contrast with other graph families supporting asynchronous recurrent cycles. The exact ten-layer synchronization-time distribution, the sharp nine-step witness for every graph order, the symmetry N_1=N_3, and concentration at time two for growing cliques are natural quantitative dynamical invariants of a two-parameter infinite family and are not routine substitutions into a pre-existing formula.
